title: Upcoming IPOs, Explained Simply — November 2026

faq.q: How do I even apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank's ASBA (Applications Supported by Blocked Amount) facility or through your demat account provider/broker's online platform. The funds are blocked in your bank account and only debited if you are allotted shares.
The lot size is the minimum number of shares you must bid for in an IPO. It ensures that shares are distributed in manageable blocks.

faq.q: What is the difference between Mainboard and SME IPOs?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger, more established companies that list on the main exchanges (NSE, BSE). SME IPOs are for smaller companies, listed on dedicated SME platforms (like NSE Emerge or BSE SME), with slightly different regulatory requirements and trading rules.
Oversubscription happens when the total demand for shares in an IPO (the number of shares applied for) is greater than the total number of shares offered by the company.

faq.q: Can I sell my shares on the listing day?
faq.a: Yes, once your allotted shares are credited to your demat account and the company's shares start trading on the stock exchange, you are free to sell them on the listing day itself.
